why: D2 batch 3 (b): the answer's dict entry hidden from one later code line at a time (names list, chain lines, print line, rest of the question, last tokens) and from unions with the last tokens, all layers, on code_pointer_v1 (animals, months)
gate: pointer sets: a (domain, family, condition) cell enters iff its clean Wilson lower bound >= 0.85 in the competence run (0.8 for alias_pointer_v1's other surface forms); a (domain, condition) group needs at least one family that looks its answer up; items: every competence prompt right; scenes paired across the group's entered families (and, in alias_pointer_v1, across the surface forms: a domain enters only with both forms); first n scenes by id
knockout:
At every layer l in a row's layer set, everything else in the model untouched:
- full (gated softmax) attention: the logits of the pairs (d, s), d in D, s in S, are -inf in every head, so d's
  softmax renormalises over the keys it may still read; every other pair, and the output gate (a function of d's own
  input), as is.
- Gated DeltaNet: the token mixer runs a second time and that run's output replaces the normal one at D only (every
  other position keeps the normal output). The gated delta rule, state_t = a_t state_{t-1} (I - b_t k_t k_t^T) +
  b_t v_t k_t^T, is linear in the values: o_t = sum_j w_tj v_j, with weights w_tj that depend on queries, keys, betas
  and decays but not on values. mode="value" (default) removes exactly the s -> t terms: in the second run
    (i)  v_s = 0 for s in S (the value after the short conv), every key, beta and decay unchanged, so no weight w_tj
         changes (beta_s = 0 instead would also drop s's erase of earlier writes, which can restore an earlier,
         template-identical statement: not an edge removal);
    (ii) S's conv taps are dropped from the value channels: the depthwise causal conv (kernel 4) mixes x_s into the
         values of the next 3 tokens, which write to the state D reads; the conv's value-channel input is zeroed at S
         (the conv is linear and bias-free before its SiLU), so those values lose exactly x_s's terms and keep the rest.
  What S keeps in "value" mode: its weights, i.e. its own key, beta and decay (how much it erases and decays what came
  before it) and its taps in the next 3 tokens' keys and queries. No content (value) of S reaches D directly.
  mode="absent" (the positive control) removes S from the recurrence altogether: conv input zeroed at S in every
  channel, beta_s = 0 and decay a_s = 1 (g_s = 0). S then has no influence at all on D's layer-l output, as if its
  tokens were not in this layer's mixer (which also undoes S's erase of earlier writes).

decision.needed: accuracy drop >= 20% and paired bootstrap 95% lower bound of acc(control) - acc(cell) >= 10%
decision.doc:
Decision rule (fixed before any 27B run; jobs/d2/*.yaml): on items whose unedited read is right, a cell (family,
source, destination, layer set, DeltaNet mode) is NEEDED if accuracy drops >= 20 points and the paired bootstrap 95% lower bound
of acc(matched control) - acc(cell) is >= 10 points (control: lookup_off for lookup, binding_off for binding, same
destination, layers, mode); NOT NEEDED if the Wilson 95% lower bound of its accuracy is >= 90%; otherwise PARTIAL.
Positive control: each family's path sources at (after, all, mode absent) must be NEEDED, or that family is not
interpreted. Claims: C1a "RL breaks, RR survives" if RL (lookup, both, all) is NEEDED and RR (lookup, both, all) NOT
NEEDED; C1b "the answer site reads the lookup statement directly" if (lookup, final, all) is NEEDED for BL and RL and
(lookup, question, all) is not; "relay" if the reverse; the band where the lookup must be visible from the final
positions: the largest L with suf L NEEDED and the smallest L with pre L NEEDED.

batch3_rules.reader: a unit (query head, key/value group, layer, whole range; a code line or union of lines) is a reader if acc(control) - acc(unit) >= 10 points and its entity-cluster bootstrap 95% lower bound >= 5 points (control: the same unit blocked from a statement of the same kind off the answer's path, the same items)
batch3_rules.relay: code: a line relays if blocking it together with the last tokens costs >= 10 points more than the last tokens alone (entity-cluster lower bound >= 5 points)
batch3_rules.explained: code: the lines explain the survivors if the union (last tokens + print + list/chain lines + the rest of the question) keeps answer org within 10 points of 'every line after the dict' (point estimate)
batch3_rules.readout: the best head is chosen on even-numbered scenes (pooled over the families that look the answer up) and scored on odd-numbered ones; it reads the pointer better than the slot probe if its entity-cluster lower bound > 39%
batch3_rules.reproduction: heads grid: memory → prompt with all late attention heads blocked at the last tokens reproduces batch 2 if its cluster interval overlaps 11%-20%
batch3_rules.multiplicity: single heads are many tests (24 heads x 4-8 layers per range): a single-head reader is read together with its key/value group and layer cells, never alone

intervals: Headline and rule intervals: entity-cluster bootstrap (the queried entities resampled with replacement within each domain, all their items kept; 4000 draws, seed 0); reported second: the item-level Wilson interval (accuracy) and the paired item bootstrap (2000 draws). Every number also per domain, with n items / k entities.
